# ASTRA: logarithmic PIT and exact realization complexity

**Research date:** 8 October 2026 (Australia/Brisbane).  
**Foundational target:** deterministic polynomial-time black-box identity testing for general polynomial-degree commutative arithmetic circuits in characteristic zero.  
**Outcome:** no resolution of this target, and no certified foundational discovery. This state contains complete representation theorems and barriers, a reconstructed hitting-set theorem that the novelty check identified as existing work, exact finite verification, and the specific remaining sufficient lemma. None of the barriers is a lower bound against arbitrary commutative circuits or arbitrary PIT algorithms.

Astra repository: `harjassand/astra-research-knowledge`, pinned at
`d20c4b040f63c2fb0c8da76362046d1946d0a2b9`.

OpenAI mathematics source repository: `openai/math`, pinned at
`fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`.

## Outcome

**This investigation did not reach the requested foundational endpoint.** The selected target was deterministic black-box polynomial identity testing for general polynomial-degree commutative arithmetic circuits. I did not obtain a proof resolving it.

The strongest complete result obtained is an **exact characterization of the linear-representation obstruction** encountered when transferring the new noncommutative identity-testing mechanism to commutative circuits. It identifies the same invariant behind weighted automata, logarithmic monodromy, and rational differential equations—and proves exponential lower bounds for that representation strategy even on simple polynomials.

**Historical novelty of that characterization is not established.** A positive hitting-set theorem reconstructed during the investigation turned out to be existing work from September 28, 2026, and has not been counted as a discovery.

The consequential mathematics, proofs, counterexamples, source-access record, and executable checks are preserved here:
